workload.name: customer-centric transaction lookup with order and date access
workload.score_formula: 70% measured weighted single-shard query coverage + 20% measured shard balance + 10% non-monotonic insert-key credit.

reason: customer_id scored highest (0.615) under the displayed workload weights using measured query plans, shard balance, and key progression. Hashed keys can improve distribution but reduce range locality; here their measured results are shown rather than assumed.

matrix.query_targeting: customer id equality: 2 shard(s); order id equality: 1 shard(s); date range: 2 shard(s); customer id range: 2 shard(s)
matrix.hotspot_risk: High: input key values increase in insert order; the active upper range is a write hotspot risk.
matrix.range_efficiency: Date range: scatter/gather; customer range: scatter/gather

transactions_by_order_id.hotspot_risk: High: input key values increase in insert order; the active upper range is a write hotspot risk.
transactions_by_order_id.fit: Best when order lookups dominate; customer and date filters scatter, and sequential IDs can make the upper range hot.

transactions_by_customer_id.hotspot_risk: Low in this dataset: values are not monotonic and the most frequent key represents 1.0% of rows.
transactions_by_customer_id.fit: Keeps customer equality/range reads local. Check hot-customer skew; this source dataset's frequency counts are measured above.

transactions_by_order_date.hotspot_risk: High: input key values increase in insert order; the active upper range is a write hotspot risk.
transactions_by_order_date.fit: Targets time windows, but increasing dates route new writes to the active upper range.

transactions_by_hashed_customer_id.hotspot_risk: Low in this dataset: values are not monotonic and the most frequent key represents 1.0% of rows.
transactions_by_hashed_customer_id.fit: Can distribute distinct customer keys and targets equality reads, but removes customer/date ordering and scatters range queries.

measurement_note: Dataset cardinality and value frequencies come from the persisted source collection. Placement, storage, write elapsed time, and query plans come from the live Chapter 11 cluster.
placement_note: The range-key collections are split at a value midpoint and the upper range is placed on the second Chapter 11 shard to make routing observable; document placement is then measured, not assumed.
